results.title: Durable self-compaction lifecycle
results.summary: Implemented the standalone @nicknisi/pi-self-compact package: the self_compact note tool with durable branch-local handoff state, batch-aware reservation plus active-tool lock and tool_call gate, idle-only compaction with a transcript system-instruction override that cancels on failure (no silent fallback), verbatim-note continuation, and reload/retry recovery; backed by unit tests, real-Pi integration tests via a faux provider, a write-boundary utility, and package-local Pi 0.86.1 pinning. All spec validation commands pass and repo-wide typecheck/lint show no regression. — Cycle 2 resolves every prior finding: print-mode and JSON-mode survival tests now drive a real `pi -p`/`pi --mode json` subprocess to completion (cli-runner.ts + cli-harness.ts), the session_compact reconciliation path gains automatic-overflow, manual `/compact`-on-reload, and queued-message coverage, the ready-to-deliver branch now sets the `busy` guard before delivering, and session_compact reconciliation is correctly scoped to the `pending` phase so a failed cycle still requires explicit retry. The implementation matches the spec's Technical Approach, Implementation Details, and Testing Requirements, follows the referenced patterns, and is ready to commit; the sole remaining note is a low-severity test-ergonomics suggestion, not a blocker.
findings: low/spec-deviation packages/self-compact/verify/cli-runner.ts:1 — Survival harness spawns the real CLI via node_modules dist/bundle/cli.js, so these tests silently require a prior package-local build to exist; if dist is absent the two survival cases fail at spawn rather than reporting a clear skip/precondition → Optionally assert the CLI bundle path exists (or document the build prerequisite) so a missing dist yields an actionable message instead of an opaque spawn failure.

results.title: Threshold controls and context UI
results.summary: Added threshold flag parsing/resolution (config.ts), the 20-cell context bar renderer (bar.ts), soft/warning/hard enforcement with a fail-closed execution gate and above-editor widget, editable soft/warning guidance templates with interpolation, --compact-prompt wiring, and the self-compact-info/self-compact-now commands, with full unit and real-Pi integration coverage. — Phase 2 is a thorough, spec-faithful implementation: pure config/bar helpers exactly reproduce the documented threshold ordering and the [###~====-!-|--------] 40% fixture, the three-level soft/warning/hard behavior with once-per-cycle guidance and a fail-closed execution gate is correctly wired, and gate ordering ensures hard enforcement never clobbers an active handoff's tool snapshot. Test coverage across config/bar/lifecycle/prompts/integration is comprehensive and the referenced statusline pattern is honored (display math only, aboveEditor widget, no footer replacement). Only three low-severity suggestions remain — all testing/robustness polish — so the implementation is ready to commit.
findings: low/testing packages/self-compact/lifecycle.test.ts:250 — The 'delivers guidance without triggering a turn' test asserts only sent().toHaveLength(1); the harness sendMessage mock discards the options object, so it cannot actually prove triggerTurn:false was passed — the core 'never restart a finished task' guarantee is unverified at unit level → Have the harness capture the send options (triggerTurn/deliverAs) and assert triggerTurn===false, or add an integration test that fires guidance while idle and asserts no new provider turn runs.

low/spec-deviation packages/self-compact/extensions/self-compact/self-compact.ts:410 — The continuation-delivery path calls clearHard() but does not call updateWidget(ctx); the spec lists 'compaction state changes, and restore' as widget-refresh triggers. A stale pre-compaction bar can briefly linger until the next turn_end/agent_settled → Call updateWidget(ctx) after clearHard() in the continuation delivery so the bar refreshes immediately on a successful cycle.

low/testing packages/self-compact/lifecycle.test.ts:99 — The lifecycle harness setWidget mock ignores the third options arg ({ placement: 'aboveEditor' }), so no test asserts the widget is registered above the editor rather than as a footer replacement (a spec 'Decisions Considered' requirement) → Assert the aboveEditor placement in at least one widget test to lock in coexistence with existing statusline footers.

results.title: Live acceptance and release integration
results.summary: Added the bounded real-model live acceptance driver (with offline self-test and fresh-continuation/reload-no-replay/completed-task scenarios, all PASS against anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 on Pi 0.86.1), packaging/manifest/standalone-load/release-integration tests, the package README, verification results, a minor changeset, and a root README row. No source-file fixes were required since existing behavior already satisfied acceptance. — The phase-3 deliverables (bounded real-model live driver, package/manifest/standalone-loading tests, portable README, RESULTS evidence, changeset, and root-README row) closely follow the spec's technical approach and referenced patterns: fail-closed version/credential/timeout gating, isolated -ne -e launches, a persistent-session reload path, ownership-guarded result.txt, no driver-side write or second prompt, and a deterministic self-test proving the four mandated wrong-behavior cases fail before any spend. Spec 'Modified Files' that don't appear are validly absent (conditioned on acceptance-driven fixes), machine-local evidence is correctly git-ignored, and the pre-existing codemode/workflows edits are left unstaged as required — they must not enter the phase commit. Ready to commit; only two low, non-blocking suggestions remain.
findings: low/spec-deviation packages/self-compact/verify/cli-harness.ts:1 — New test-harness extension is not listed in the spec's File Changes table, though it is required by the CLI-survival check (consumed by verify/cli-runner.ts and integration.test.ts's 'print/JSON survival' block) and is correctly excluded from the packed release by the files allowlist → Acceptable per the spec's CLI-survival requirement; record it in the run notes / File Changes list for traceability.

low/spec-deviation packages/self-compact/verify/live.mjs:parseEvents — collectEvidence reduces the JSON stream by event type only and does not correlate command/response IDs as Implementation Detail #3 suggests → Optional: correlate request/response IDs to tighten evidence; the existing timeout + explicit-evidence gating already prevents treating a quiet timeout as success, so this is non-blocking.
